newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-LIBERIAN STRIKERS COULD HOLD KEY TO FRENCH CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIBERIAN STRIKERS COULD HOLD KEY TO FRENCH CUP FINAL.

text.p: The French Cup Final between Nice and Guingamp on Saturday could hinge on the scoring talents of two Liberians at the very ground where their compatriot George Weah made his name.

Nice striker James Debbah and Guingamp's Christopher Wreh come face to face at the Parc des Princes where Weah displayed his skills for Paris St Germain before going on to become European and world footballer of the year with AC Milan.
Debbah has scored two goals in the competition and Wreh three, including the crucial first in Guingamp's 2-0 extra-time victory over Montpellier in the semifinals.
The Nice striker has been out of action since March after injuring his eye in the quarter-final at Clermond but the Cote d'Azur club have been working overtime to get him fit for the final.

The 25th final at the Parc -- the last before it hands over to the new Stade de France at St Denis the other side of Paris next year -- may lack a big-name team but what they lack in glamour the two sides and their fans make up for in commitment.
The Parc will be packed with a sellout 48,000 crowd and awash with the black and red of two clubs with the same colours. Nice will play the final in white.
Nice are hoping to ease the pain of league relegation by winning the cup for the third time. Should they do so, they will play in the European Cup Winners' Cup as a second division side.
They last won a trophy during their 1950s glory days when they lifted the league title four times and the cup twice.
Guingamp, a top-flight club for only two seasons, have never previously gone beyond the quarter-finals.
They expect 12,000 fans at the Parc -- more than the entire population of 8,700 in their small Brittany town.
Nice, having raised the city's hopes of a first trophy in nearly 40 years, will play in front of more fans, some 10,000, than at any home game this season.

"We'll have to be strong defensively and know how to mark their two or three danger men... We know it will be tight, it will be tactical and we'll pay for the slightest mistake," Nice midfielder Frederic Gioria said.
Nice have won the race to get Debbah fit, while Guingamp are confident they will be able to field Monaco-bound playmaker Stephane Carnot, who has been nursing an injured thigh.
But whereas Guingamp's key defender Jerome Foulon appears ready to play, veteran Jean-Philippe Mattio, who has been at Nice since 1984, has lost his battle for fitness.
There is also disappointment for Nice's Serbian midfielder Zoran Milinkovic, who has been left out of the squad because of a cup rule allowing only two non-European Union players per team.
Nice coach Silvester Takac, making what he called a painful and difficult decision, has opted instead for Pole Andrezj Kubica as Debbah's partner in attack.
Takac says his team can draw strength from their position as underdogs. "That could be an asset. It's interesting because that means you want to cause a surprise.

"There's also certainly the handicap of a Debbah who will not be able to play at 100 percent, even though his latest eye tests have been positive, because we mustn't forget he missed four weeks of training."
Takac said that despite Guingamp's reputation for not being an attractive side, he thought them very effective.
"They have two stoppers who are hard to pass, there is quality in the middle and don't forget Wreh, a constant danger. They're very solid," he said.
The two evenly-matched teams have even shared their league points this season. Guingamp won 2-1 at Nice in August, while the Cote d'Azur club won 1-0 when they came north to Brittany in December.
Probable teams:

Guingamp - Angelo Hugues; Jerome Foulon, Richard Lecomte, Marek Jozwiak, Gheorghe Mihali; Yannick Baret, Claude Michel, Charles-Edouard Coridon, Stephane Carnot; Christophe Horlaville, Christopher Wreh.
Nice - Bruno Valencony; Youssef Salimi, Olivier Fugen, Thierry Cretier, Bruno Calegari; Frederic Tatarian, Thierry de Neef, Roberto Onorati, Mohamed Chaouch; Andrezj Kubica, James Debbah.
